title: Modi Opens ESTIC 2026, Urges India to Create Technologies, Not Just Adopt Them
excerpt: Inaugurating the three-day science conclave at Bharat Mandapam, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said a developed India will rest on original research, as ministers pointed to a Rs 1 lakh crore innovation fund and a startup count that has risen from 350 to 250,000.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated ESTIC 2026, the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on October 27.
  • Modi said India must move from adopting foreign technologies to creating original ones, citing its COVID-19 vaccines, first-attempt Mars mission and Moon south-pole landing.
  • The three-day conclave, running October 27 to 29, covers 12 thematic areas and features about 150 deep-tech startup stalls and three Nobel laureates.
  • Science Minister Jitendra Singh said India's startups have grown from 350 to 250,000 in 12 to 13 years, backed by a Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Fund.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday inaugurated the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, telling scientists, policymakers, industry leaders, startup founders and students that a developed India would be built on original research rather than borrowed technology.

"India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly, and lead the world in creating them," Modi said, according to coverage of the address. He said India is moving from adopting technologies developed elsewhere to creating new technologies and developing solutions to global challenges.

From follower to co-creator

Modi cited India's indigenous COVID-19 vaccines and its large-scale vaccination drive, its first-attempt Mars mission and the landing near the Moon's uncharted south pole as evidence of a changed technological mindset. He also highlighted the indigenous 500-megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor achieving first criticality a few months ago, describing it as a major step toward long-term strength in nuclear energy and reduced dependence on imported nuclear fuel.

Science and Technology Minister Jitendra Singh said India was "no longer a follower, now a global co-creator." Singh said that since the announcement of the Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Fund, the startup ecosystem had grown from 350 to 250,000 startups, placing India third globally. The space economy had expanded to $9 billion, he said, and the bio-economy from $10 billion to nearly $200 billion.

"Our ranking in the Global Innovation Index has improved from 80th to 38th. The number of patents had increased from 42,763 to 1,10,375, representing a rise of 158 per cent."

— Jitendra Singh, Minister of State for Science and Technology

Singh added that India now ranks third globally in the number of science PhDs, compared with seventh earlier.

What the conclave covers

The three-day conclave, scheduled from October 27 to 29, will deliberate on 12 thematic areas including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate science and ocean research, according to the official programme summary. A technology exhibition will showcase indigenous scientific achievements, with around 150 deep-tech startups presenting through dedicated stalls.

Three Nobel laureates — Joachim Frank, Sir Richard J. Roberts and Kostya Novoselov — are among the eminent faculty. A Global Connect Networking Event will bring together more than 300 invited participants from academia, research institutions and industry in India and abroad to explore research partnerships and pathways from laboratories to markets. ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said the space agency will display a model of a proposed heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of placing over 30,000 kg into low Earth orbit.

What to watch

The test of the conclave's message is translation: whether the innovation fund reaches laboratories and startups quickly enough to convert India's improved patent and publication numbers into products in AI, semiconductors, space and nuclear energy. For Indian researchers and founders abroad, those funding and partnership channels — on show at Bharat Mandapam through October 29 — are the practical route into India's research push. Deliberations continue through Thursday, with thematic sessions setting research priorities for the year ahead.
